images.title: Trilobite (Cambrian)
images.description: A detailed reconstruction of a Cambrian trilobite, Paradoxides, swimming above the muddy seafloor in warm, shallow tropical seas.

images.title: Anomalocaris canadensis
images.description: Anomalocaris, the apex predator of the Cambrian seas, sweeping its grasping frontal appendages toward a cluster of trilobites.

images.title: Dunkleosteus terrelli
images.description: The massive armored placoderm Dunkleosteus terrelli, its bony scissor jaws agape, dominating the Late Devonian seas.

images.title: Carboniferous Coal Forest
images.description: A lush Carboniferous coal swamp forest with towering Lepidodendron lycopod trees, giant horsetails, and a giant dragonfly gliding through the humid air.

images.title: Dimetrodon grandis
images.description: Dimetrodon grandis, a large sail-backed pelycosaur synapsid, basking on a rocky Early Permian floodplain with its impressive dorsal sail raised to absorb heat.

images.title: Lystrosaurus murrayi
images.description: A herd of the stocky, pig-like dicynodont therapsid Lystrosaurus foraging in the sparse, recovering vegetation of the Early Triassic aftermath.

images.title: Ophthalmosaurus icenicus
images.description: Ophthalmosaurus, a dolphin-shaped Jurassic ichthyosaur with its distinctive enormous eyes, leaping from a warm Mesozoic sea.

images.title: Brachiosaurus altithorax
images.description: A towering Brachiosaurus altithorax stretches its long neck into the high canopy of a Late Jurassic conifer forest, while a smaller Stegosaurus grazes in the background.

images.title: Quetzalcoatlus northropi
images.description: The colossal azhdarchid pterosaur Quetzalcoatlus northropi strides across a Late Cretaceous floodplain, its eleven-meter wingspan held half-open as it scans for prey.

images.title: Tyrannosaurus rex
images.description: Tyrannosaurus rex, feathered along its back and neck, stalking through a Late Cretaceous floodplain forest with a dramatic sunset sky behind it.

images.title: Mosasaurus hoffmannii
images.description: The enormous marine lizard Mosasaurus hoffmannii bursting through the surface of the Late Cretaceous Western Interior Seaway, jaws wide open around an ammonite.

images.title: Pakicetus inachus
images.description: Pakicetus inachus, the early wolf-like whale ancestor, wading into an Eocene river to catch fish, its hoofed feet still visible beneath the water.
